newsitem.title: USA: Central Vermont to appeal N.H. deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Central Vermont to appeal N.H. deregulation.

text.p: Central Vermont Public Service Corp said Wednesday it will appeal a ruling by the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission (PUC) which prevents recovery of any stranded costs as the Granite state moved toward deregulation of its electric industry.
Central Vermont said it stands to lose $80 million over 28 years if a PUC order on stranded costs tied to the utility's wholly-owned subsidiary Connecticut Valley Electric Co is allowed to stand.
"Without some sort of intervention, we could have to write off $2.6 million -- before taxes -- in the first quarter of this year," said Central Vermont spokesman Steve Costello.
Costello said the PUC's order denies recovery of costs associated with Connecticut Valley's contract to buy about 20 megawatts of electricity annually from Central Vermont.
"Basically, they're saying that Connecticut Valley shouldn't have signed the contract with us," Costello said.
But Central Vermont argues that the contract was approved by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and that New Hampshire has exceeded its jurisdiction.
FERC officials did not return phone calls seeking comment.
But NHPUC executive director Thomas Getz said from his Concord, N.H. offices, "We clearly believe we do have the jurisdiction and if they want to go to FERC, we'll down there too and argue it."

Connecticut Valley Electric provides about 28 megawatts of power to some 10,000 New Hampshire customers, two-thirds of which is supplied under a contract with its parent company based in Rutland, Vermont.
Costello said that under the contract, which has been renewed annually since 1948, "Connecticut Valley has enjoyed a $60 million savings in below market rates."
